title: model-loading-weights-shard-incident-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Encountered intermittent model load failures on dedicated cluster when pulling checkpoint for model: redwood/optic-13B-2026-02 (quantized + sharded)
- Failures started after nightly snapshot sync (2026-02-24 23:40 UTC)
- Symptoms: 1) loader hangs ~30s then fails; 2) deterministic failure when loading specific worker pod (node-7)

What I saw (local repro notes):
- Attempted to load locally after downloading shards from GCS. Some shards download OK, others are truncated.
- Commands tried:
    $ gsutil -m cp gs://redwood-checkpoints/optic-13B-2026-02/shard-* ./shards/
    $ sha256sum shard-0 shard-1 shard-2 shard-3
    $ wc -c shard-*
    $ file shard-3

- Example errors during python load: 
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      File "loader.py", line 132, in <module>
        state = torch.load(f, map_location='cpu')
    EOFError: Ran out of input

    OR

    RuntimeError: unexpected EOF while reading file

- Serving runtime logs (relevant excerpts):
    2026-02-25T02:03:41Z [node-7] WARN model_loader: shard download failed: HTTP 206 partial content, expected bytes 0-1073741823, got 0-32767
    2026-02-25T02:03:42Z [node-7] ERROR model_loader: checksum mismatch for shard-3 (expected a3f5..., actual 5b2e...)
    2026-02-25T02:03:42Z [node-7] ERROR model_loader: mark shard-3 bad; falling back to smaller variant

Hypotheses (ordered by likelihood):
1) Partial/Truncated download during sync: multi-part upload or interrupted transfer left a corrupted shard in GCS.
   - Evidence: wc -c shows shard-3 smaller than others, EOF errors, HTTP 206 ranges weird.
2) Checkpoint writing pipeline bug: snapshotter wrote incomplete shard due to OOM or premature termination on the builder machine.
   - Evidence: snapshot logs around 2026-02-24 23:38 show "rsync: write failed: No space left on device" on builder-2 (need to validate).
3) Checkpoint format mismatch (safetensors vs torch .pt) / conversion step failed for one shard producing garbage bytes.
   - Evidence: file(1) reports "data" for shard-3 while others show "gzip compressed data" (we used compression in pipeline)
4) CDN/edge caching serving stale/incomplete ranges to some nodes (node-7 hitting different edge).

What I've tried so far (and results):
- Re-downloaded shards to local host using gsutil (same truncated file persists) -> suggests source in GCS is corrupted.
- Verified object metadata via GCS console (size mismatch; upload timestamp 2026-02-24T23:39) -> matches problematic window.
- Tried curl with range resume: curl -C - -o shard-3.partial "https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-checkpoints/.../shard-3" -> server returns "HTTP/1.1 416 Range Not Satisfiable" for resumed ranges.
- Ran safetensors validator (for safetensors format) -> errors (but model is supposed to be torch .pt, so validator irrelevant but checked as sanity)
- Attempted to load with safetensors library (to check format) -> UnpicklingError when treating as torch, binary blob when treated as safetensors -> indicates corruption not format mismatch only.
- Cross-checked with blobstore service (internal) -> object has same size in GS; object version history shows only one upload.

Quick checks to run (next):
- Download shard-3 to a fresh GCE instance in same region as storage bucket (reduce network path variance) and compare sha256 to local copy.
- Try gsutil hash -m to compute checksum reported by GCS (compare to expected from release manifest).
- Pull builder VM (builder-2) logs for the snapshot job around 23:30-23:45; look for rsync/oom/disk errors.
- Run `gsutil cp` to a different project/zone to ensure not a regional storage glitch.
- Re-run `rclone copy` (different transport) to confirm corruption is on server side.

Potential mitigations for production (short-term):
- Failover to smaller model variant (we already had fallback policy): increase traffic to fallback until checkpoint fix.
- Block node-7 from pulling new checkpoints temporarily if it's repeatedly hitting corrupt object (but this is a band-aid).
- Recreate snapshot from previous healthy snapshot (2026-02-23) and roll back serving until fix is validated.

Notes on checksums/manifest: 
- Release manifest (manifests/optic-13B-2026-02.json) lists shard sizes and sha256 sums. Need to fetch and compare.
- If manifest missing or generated incorrectly, we should detect by comparing manifest-expected checksums to actual objects.

Potential root cause timeline (draft):
- 23:30: Snapshot job starts on builder-2.
- 23:38: builder-2 disk pressure -> rsync fails for last shard write -> uploader exits but marks job success incorrectly.
- 23:39: Upload of shard-3 completes with truncated file size (server-side) -> GCS object present but corrupted.
- 23:40: Auto-sync pushes manifest referencing expected sha256 of correct full shard (manifest generated from partial state?) -> mismatch later detected when loaders compute sha256.

Relevant tickets / PRs:
- JIRA-INF-9342: initial alert and incident page (assigned to Jordan)
- gh://redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/487: added extra logging for shard download failures (PR landed today)

Immediate action items (owner tags):
- Camila: grab builder-2 snapshot logs + rsync/stdout (by EOD 2026-03-01)
- Jordan: run gsutil hash -m on shard-3 and paste output into ticket (in-progress)
- Ethan: validate rollback snapshot and try to stage re-upload of full checkpoint to a staging bucket (blocked on size policy)
- Infra: check GCS object change history + any relevant maintenance windows (ask infra-eng)

Longer-term fixes to consider:
- Improve snapshot atomicity: write to tmp prefix then rename/manifest publish after all shards verified.
- Add post-upload verification step computing checksum and failing job if mismatch.
- Add automatic reingest/retry of corrupted shards from builder snapshot if available.
- Add more robust uploader that ensures multi-part uploads complete and retries on partial failures.

Random notes / breadcrumbs for future search: 
- grep for "HTTP 206" and "checksum mismatch" in model_loader logs (serving-runtime) -> points to node-7 and node-12 bursts on same night
- Look into gcs transfer logs: transferService shows 2026-02-24 23:39 as last write from builder-2 10.2.3.12

If someone picks this up: start by verifying shard-3 hash in GCS vs manifest. If GCS copy is corrupt, we need to reupload full shard from builder snapshot or restore from backup snapshot.

-- Camila
